clue.text: Rat from sandy area about to come up

parts.note: a desert is a vast sandy area

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word for about is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A rat scurries away from a stretch of sand, about to emerge from below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns RE into ER, which follows DESERT. 'Rat' is a verb-like noun here: someone who deserts their side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a turncoat who abandons comrades, just like a runaway soldier.

indicators.note: potential suggests these letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is cleared of any hidden capability they might have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' is the anagram signal working on the eight letters of 'of secret'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off without punishment is to be released unharmed, an idiom for being let off.

clue.text: Little woman may approve of those without work

definitions.note: a plural phrase, matching the adjective used as a collective noun, as in 'the unemployed'

parts.note: Jo March is a heroine of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
to bless something is to give it approval

explanation.surface: A small lady might give her blessing to the unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: JO is Jo March of Little Women, so 'Little woman' is a literary nod rather than a short female.
explanation.definitionFit: People out of employment are collectively called the unemployed, as in 'help for the workless'.

explanation.surface: A two-word note on a workplace romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Business: a matter or concern, as in 'that's my own concern'; relationship: a romantic liaison, often secret.

clue.text: Team, it is reported, sounded unhappy

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for team is taken by its sound

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A sports team is said to have been audibly disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale long and audibly is how one expresses sadness or weariness.

parts.note: a schism in a church could be read as a rupture in belief itself, the phrase for breaking a promise

explanation.definitionFit: Breaking trust or a pledge is literally a crack in one's faithfulness, which a church schism also is.

explanation.surface: A lonely figure who may also be furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, being next to yourself means no one else is there, hence alone; the idiom means frantic with emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone: read literally, standing at your own side with no company; angry perhaps: the idiom for being overcome by rage or distress.

parts.note: a tale of misfortune, told to win sympathy, is literally an unlucky narrative

explanation.definitionFit: A tale of misfortune told to gain pity is a sob story about bad breaks.

clue.text: What dog is pursuing on the way up?

explanation.surface: A hound follows a trail as it climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, a dog follows 'a scent'; as one word it is a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: What dog is pursuing: a smell or trail, read as two words; the way up: a climb or upward slope.

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassy field

explanation.surface: A rugged patch of meadow lies beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat or skin that is hard and chewy is likened to hide, i.e. tough.

indicators.note: stopping short means the word ends early, losing its final letter

parts.note: to feel is to touch

explanation.surface: Someone touches a bill but stops before paying it.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge for professional services is a sum paid.

indicators.note: helter-skelter means in wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A journalist rides along in a hectic rush.
explanation.walkthrough: A helter-skelter is also a spiral fairground slide in Britain, which suits 'ride'.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a paper's content is the senior journalist who runs it.

clue.text: Sit astride right back in the seat

indicators.note: in means the turned letters go inside the seat word

parts.note: a saddle is a rider's seat

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for right is turned around

explanation.surface: Someone takes the correct place on a saddle by sitting properly back in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RT into TR, and 'in' puts it inside SADDLE after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to have one leg on each side, a synonym for sitting astride.

explanation.surface: A two-word pairing of drying and song.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry: to air washing is to dry it out; music: a tune or melody.

indicators.note: pronouncedly asks for the word as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: coarser means less refined or rougher

explanation.surface: A dog is unmistakably more uncouth.
explanation.walkthrough: A courser is a hound bred for coursing, chasing hares by sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A courser is a hunting hound used for chasing game by sight, such as a greyhound.

clue.text: Runner appearing twice in luxurious kidskin!

indicators.note: the letters run across the words and occur twice, in luxurious-kidskin and inside kidskin itself

explanation.surface: A runner shows up twice in a fancy goatskin leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across luxuriouS KIdskin and again within kidSKIn.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner fixed under a boot for gliding over snow, like a sledge runner.

explanation.surface: A man looms above an oil well.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow: a man's first name, a typical male name; towering over oil-well: the tall framework built above a drilling site.

parts.note: crabs scuttle sideways, so a crab-like motion is a sideways one, not a bad-tempered one

explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways, the way a crab scuttles, is moving side-first.

indicators.note: headed means only the first letter of the word red is taken

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired cleric is healthy and dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red-headed' looks like a description of the priest, but 'headed' takes just the R of 'Red'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependable can be relied on, which is what trustworthy means.

clue.text: Cup finalist bound to be supple

indicators.note: finalist means the last letter of the word cup

parts.note: liable means bound or obliged

explanation.surface: A cup final team is required to be agile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup finalist' reads as a sports team, but it is the final letter of 'Cup'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supple bends easily, a synonym for flexible.

clue.text: Against rewriting article going straight up

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters of the word article are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone opposes the redrafting of a piece that goes straight up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' makes ERTICAL from ARTICLE, which follows V.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright and perpendicular to the horizon means rising straight upwards.

clue.text: Upsetting experience, a tram crashing with you said to be inside

indicators.note: inside means that letter goes within the jumbled letters
crashing means the letters of a tram are thrown into disorder
said to be means the word you is taken by its sound, a single letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U

explanation.surface: A tram crash with you in it would be a shocking ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' turns A TRAM into TRAMA; 'said to be' makes YOU into U, and 'inside' places it to give TRA-U-MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A deeply distressing event that leaves lasting psychological harm is a shock.

clue.text: Elevation in Cyprus that's rather cold

indicators.note: in means the elevation word sits inside the code for Cyprus

parts.note: CY is the international vehicle code for Cyprus
a hill is a raised piece of ground

explanation.surface: A hilltop on Cyprus can get quite cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat cold weather is described as cool or nippy.

indicators.note: into means the look word goes inside the cut word

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone examines a tear in a rubber overshoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber boot worn over a shoe in wet weather is also called a galosh.

clue.text: Fish thought to have lost its tail

indicators.note: losing its tail means the word for thought drops its final letter

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A fish is believed to be missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thought' looks like a verb (believed), but it is the noun IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family, also called the orfe.

clue.text: The man Patrick in charge of one plant

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Pat is a short form of Patrick
a means one

explanation.surface: A man named Patrick is put in charge of a single plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatica is a woodland flower of the buttercup family with liver-shaped leaves.

clue.text: We have a poncho, not half, only an arm

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word poncho is used, its first three letters

explanation.surface: We have half a poncho, only enough to cover one arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb in the poncho picture but means a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, so a single arm is one item of weaponry.

parts.note: a bond that matters to relatives, the kind that binds kin together, not a necktie

explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance among relations is the bond that matters among kin.
